messages.subject: ezAnova without error but the result are strange
messages.subject_clean: ezAnova without error but the result are strange
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone:

　　I'm trying to solve a data with multiple level nested repeat measurement, the data set is in attachment. What I want to do is compare "two different site" of oocytes number, I have "2" site, each site have "5" colony, in each colony I pickup "3" polyp which with "10~12" measurement(is this the repeat measurement?).I did the ezAnova without alarm of unbalance, but the result were all NAN........

Here is my code:

rt_anova = ezANOVA(
    data = data
  , dv = value
  , wid = Site
  , within = .(Col,polyp)
  , between = Site
)

print(rt_anova)

and result:
$ANOVA
          Effect      DFn DFd   F   p p<.05 ges
2           Site        1   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
3            Col        4   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
5          polyp       2   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
4       Site:Col      4   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
6     Site:polyp     2   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
7      Col:polyp     8   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
8 Site:Col:polyp   8   0 NaN NaN    NA   1

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I also did another way that I average all measurement within the polyp, that means now I have "2" site, each site have "5" colony, in each colony with "3" polyp measurement(within subject?)

and my code become like this:

data1=ddply(data,.(subnum,Site,Col,polyp),summarize,mean=mean(value))

rt_anova = ezANOVA(
    data = data1
  , dv = mean
  , wid = Site
  , within = .(Col,polyp)
  , between = Site
)

print(rt_anova)

But the result are same:

$ANOVA
          Effect DFn DFd   F   p p<.05 ges
2           Site   1   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
3            Col   4   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
5          polyp   2   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
4       Site:Col   4   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
6     Site:polyp   2   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
7      Col:polyp   8   0 NaN NaN    NA   1
8 Site:Col:polyp   8   0 NaN NaN    NA   1

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I really have no idea why the result show like this, I'm appreciate your attention!

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] ezAnova without error but the result are strange
messages.subject_clean: [ez4r] ezAnova without error but the result are strange
messages.body_plain:
You can't use the same variable as a within identifier (wid) and a between variable. What it seems to me is that you actually fully between design where colony is the unit of observation within which you have no manipulated variables but you do have multiple measures per colony. ezANOVA isn't able to handle such data in raw format (i.e. taking advantage of the multiple measures per colony), but it will automatically aggregate the multiple measures per colony to a mean for you if you set it up correctly. You first have to create a variable that encodes a unique identifier per colony across your between variable (site):

    data$colony = factor(paste(data$Col,data$Site))

Now you can do:

my_anova = ezANOVA(

    data = data
    , dv = value

    , wid = colony

    , between = Site
)

Alternatively, a non-ez method of analysis that uses all the information in the raw data, including variance of the multiple measures per colony would be:

    library(lme4)
    data$colony = factor(paste(data$Col,data$Site))
    fit = lmer(
        data = data
        , formula = value ~ Site + (1|colony)
    )
    print(fit) #show coefficients
    coef(fit,method='wald') #show confidence intervals on coefficients

Now, this all assumes that you are interested in evaluating the influence of site on your measure.

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.body_plain:
I'm not sure whether the Mauchley correction applies here. I've not seen it in this context of multiple replicates per cell. However, by analogy you can deal with the underlying problem by accounting for the allowing random slopes as well as intercepts.

  library(lme4)
    data$colony = factor(paste(data$Col,data$Site))
    fit = lmer(
        data = data

        , formula = value ~ Site + (Site|colony)

    )
    print(fit) #show coefficients
    coef(fit,method='wald') #show confidence intervals on coefficients

These sorts of models don't always converge and it may be sensible to try simpler ones such as:

  library(lme4)
    data$colony = factor(paste(data$Col,data$Site))
    fit = lmer(
        data = data

        , formula = value ~ Site + (Site||colony)

    )
    print(fit) #show coefficients
    coef(fit,method='wald') #show confidence intervals on coefficients

or

  library(lme4)
    data$colony = factor(paste(data$Col,data$Site))
    fit = lmer(
        data = data

        , formula = value ~ Site + (0 + Site||colony)

    )
    print(fit) #show coefficients
    coef(fit,method='wald') #show confidence intervals on coefficients

Thom
